$comment: WHAT A DIAGNOSIS WITNESSES (kb/Work PB5597, branch review R1-1; DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md section 10.6),
read by lineage_reads.EvidenceTable. A conformance-suite case that a compiler is to REFUSE at an edition (a refusal
test's wiseowl/diagnostics refuse-at, a flagged case's flag at) shows a diagnosis, nothing else. It witnesses an older
rule only where what the rule asks of a compiler IS a diagnosis: the rule's catalog `kind` is a key of
`diagnosed-kinds`, or the next-edition rule it carries into is `declined-verdict` (the compiler declines the
facility, and the read states the older text's licence to decline it, licence-<year>). Every other rule (a general
rule, an argument or returned-value rule, an implementor-defined item) needs a case ACCEPTED at the edition: a program
that runs there and whose output the gate compares. The keys are the catalog's own `kind`s, checked against it at load.

diagnosed-kinds.SR: a syntax rule states what a conforming program may write: a program can violate it, and the compiler satisfies it by diagnosing the violation
diagnosed-kinds.FMT: a general format states the syntax a program may write: a program outside it is diagnosed
